caption:
The biggest AI stories of the week:
Google opened Gemini 4 Argon to paying users and it topped the Vals Index.
Zuckerberg said Meta was ready to write a $100 billion to $200 billion check for AI.
Anthropic told IPO investors it made $16.8 billion in the third quarter.
Microsoft says MAI-Base-2 beat OpenAI's base model with a quarter of the compute.
Claude traced the origin of the NSA's 26-year-old mystery curve seeds.
404 Media showed ChatGPT ads can target you by email and phone number.

Which story mattered most to you?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: VentureBeat, Cheeky Pint, Reuters, Business Insider, Anthropic, Gizmodo

slides.heading: Gemini 4 Argon *goes public*
paras: Google opened Gemini 4 Argon to paying users and developers. It ranked first on the independent Vals Index, ahead of Claude Opus 5.5.
Developers pay an introductory $2 and $10 per million tokens until November 30.

slides.heading: Zuckerberg's *$200 billion* check
paras: On the Cheeky Pint podcast, Mark Zuckerberg said Meta was ready to write a check for "$100 billion, $200 billion" for AI.
"In order for it not to work out, it's not just that we have to fail, AI overall has to fail," he said.

slides.heading: Anthropic's *$16.8 billion* quarter
paras: Anthropic told would-be IPO investors it brought in $16.8 billion in the third quarter, about 45% more than the quarter before, Bloomberg and Reuters reported.
Anthropic has not published the figures and declined to comment.

slides.heading: Microsoft takes a *swing at OpenAI*
paras: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman told employees MAI-Base-2 is a stronger base model than the one behind OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol, trained with one quarter of the compute.
The comparison comes from Microsoft's own private tests.

slides.heading: Claude solves a *26-year-old* NSA puzzle
paras: Anthropic says an internal Claude model traced the NSA-supplied seeds behind NIST's ECDSA curves to an ordinary 1990s C random number generator, in under 30 minutes.
Anthropic says this is not a break of ECDSA.

slides.heading: ChatGPT ads *know your email*
paras: A 404 Media test showed advertisers can target ChatGPT users by uploading email addresses, phone numbers or Android ad IDs.
OpenAI says audiences need at least 25,000 matched users and advertisers never see who matched.

slides.hook: Six stories, one week, and AI is moving faster than ever. Follow so you never miss a week like this.
